s: Armour-Dial Inc. announced in 1966 that it would expand its product line to include aerosol cans and roll-on deodorants as well as shaving creams under the Dial brand. Thanks to Dial soap's strong sales, driven by magazine, radio, and television ads, Armour's consumer products business was established as Armour-Dial Inc. in 1967. The newly introduced Dial products, including a shampoo, were well-received, leading Greyhound Corporation to acquire Armour in 1970 and rebrand the consumer products division as Armour-Dial. The construction of a new Dial soap production plant in Aurora, Illinois, was completed in 1971.
